title: Criterion for a property of morphisms to descend along fpqc coverings (Stacks 02KP, fpqc case)
statement:
Let $\mathcal P$ be a class of morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme] satisfying the following four conditions.
(0) (Invariance under isomorphism.) If $f:X\to S$ has $\mathcal P$ and $\tilde f:\tilde X\to\tilde S$ is a morphism for which there are isomorphisms of schemes $a:X\to\tilde X$, $b:S\to\tilde S$ with $\tilde f\circ a=b\circ f$, then $\tilde f$ has $\mathcal P$.
(1) (Stable under flat base change.) If $f:X\to S$ has $\mathcal P$ and $g:S'\to S$ is a flat morphism [def-weil-flat-morphism], then the second projection $X\times_SS'\to S'$ of the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product] has $\mathcal P$.
(2) (Zariski local on the base.) If $f:X\to S$ is a morphism and $S=\bigcup_{k\in K}V_k$ is a covering of $S$ by open subschemes such that for every $k$ the restriction $f^{-1}(V_k)\to V_k$ of $f$ (a morphism from the open subscheme $f^{-1}(V_k)$ of $X$ to the open subscheme $V_k$ of $S$) has $\mathcal P$, then $f$ has $\mathcal P$.
(3) (Descent along faithfully flat morphisms of affine schemes.) If $S$ and $S'$ are affine schemes, $g:S'\to S$ is a flat and surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism] morphism, and $f:X\to S$ is a morphism such that the second projection $X\times_SS'\to S'$ has $\mathcal P$, then $f$ has $\mathcal P$.
Then for every morphism of schemes $f:X\to S$ and every fpqc covering $\{g_i:S_i\to S\}_{i\in I}$ of $S$ [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering] such that for every $i\in I$ the second projection $f_i:X\times_SS_i\to S_i$ has $\mathcal P$, the morphism $f$ has $\mathcal P$.

source.place: Descent, Lemma Tag 02KP (lemma-descending-properties-morphisms, line 5407) with tau = fpqc, the direction 'each base change has P => f has P' of 'fpqc local on the base' (Definition Tag 02KO, definition-property-morphisms-local, line 5310); its proof ('details omitted') goes through Topologies, Definition Tag 022B (topologies-definition-fpqc-covering, topologies.tex line 2888) and Lemma Tag 022E (topologies-lemma-fpqc-affine, topologies.tex line 3151: an fpqc covering of an affine scheme is refined by a finite fpqc covering by affine opens of the members). Condition (0) is the standing convention of Definition 02KO ('we see (or require) that property P holds for X -> Y iff it holds for any arrow isomorphic to it').

proof.text: *Setting and reduction to an affine open of the base.* Let $f:X\to S$ and the fpqc covering $\{g_i:S_i\to S\}_{i\in I}$ [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering] be as in the statement, with $f_i:X\times_SS_i\to S_i$ the second projections of the fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product], all having $\mathcal P$. The affine opens $U\subseteq S$ cover $S$ [def-pc-scheme]. For such $U$ write $X_U=f^{-1}(U)$ (an open subscheme of $X$) and $f_U:X_U\to U$ for the restriction of $f$. By condition (2), applied to the covering of $S$ by all its affine opens, it suffices to prove: *for every affine open $U\subseteq S$, $f_U$ has $\mathcal P$.* Steps 2-6 prove this for a fixed affine open $U$; step 7 concludes.

proof.text: *Finitely many affine opens of the members covering $U$ (Topologies 022E).* By the definition of an fpqc covering [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering], applied to the affine open $U$, there are $n\ge0$, indices $i_1,\dots,i_n\in I$ and affine opens $V_j\subseteq S_{i_j}$ ($j=1,\dots,n$) with $\bigcup_{j=1}^ng_{i_j}(V_j)=U$; in particular $g_{i_j}(V_j)\subseteq U$. Let $e_j:V_j\hookrightarrow S_{i_j}$ be the inclusion of the open subscheme and $h_j:V_j\to U$ the morphism with $(U\hookrightarrow S)\circ h_j=g_{i_j}\circ e_j$ (it exists because $g_{i_j}e_j$ has image in the open $U$, and an open subscheme $U\subseteq S$ is the open subscheme $(U,\mathcal O_S|_U)$, through which a morphism with image in $U$ factors uniquely [def-pc-scheme]). This is the refinement of Topologies, Lemma 022E, which the source proves 'directly from the definition', as here.

source.place: Topologies, Definition Tag 022B (topologies-definition-fpqc-covering, line 2888) and Lemma Tag 022E (topologies-lemma-fpqc-affine, line 3151, 'follows directly from the definition')

proof.text: *One faithfully flat morphism of affine schemes $h:U'\to U$.* Let $U'=\coprod_{j=1}^nV_j$ be the coproduct of schemes, with coprojections $\iota_j:V_j\to U'$, which are open immersions with pairwise disjoint images covering $U'$ [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]; $U'$ is affine as a finite disjoint union of affine schemes (clause (4) of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence]; for $n=0$, $U'=\emptyset=\operatorname{Spec}0$ and $U=\emptyset$). Let $h:U'\to U$ be the morphism with $h\circ\iota_j=h_j$ (universal property of the coproduct). (a) $h$ is surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism]: the image of $h$ is $\bigcup_jh_j(V_j)=\bigcup_jg_{i_j}(V_j)=U$ by step 2. (b) $h$ is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism]: let $u\in U'$, so $u=\iota_j(v)$ for some $j$ and $v\in V_j$. Since $\iota_j$, $e_j$ and $U\hookrightarrow S$ are open immersions [def-weil-open-immersion], they induce isomorphisms of local rings $\mathcal O_{U',u}\cong\mathcal O_{V_j,v}$, $\mathcal O_{V_j,v}\cong\mathcal O_{S_{i_j},e_j(v)}$ and $\mathcal O_{U,h(u)}\cong\mathcal O_{S,h(u)}$, under which the local homomorphism $\mathcal O_{U,h(u)}\to\mathcal O_{U',u}$ of $h$ becomes the local homomorphism $\mathcal O_{S,g_{i_j}(e_j(v))}\to\mathcal O_{S_{i_j},e_j(v)}$ of $g_{i_j}$ (the local homomorphisms compose along $h\iota_j=h_j$ and $(U\hookrightarrow S)h_j=g_{i_j}e_j$). The latter is flat because $g_{i_j}$ is flat (every member of an fpqc covering is flat [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]); so $h$ is flat at $u$. Thus $h:U'\to U$ is a flat surjective morphism of affine schemes.

source.place: Topologies, Definition Tag 022B (topologies-definition-fpqc-covering, line 2888) and Lemma Tag 022E (topologies-lemma-fpqc-affine, line 3151, 'follows directly from the definition')

proof.text: *The base change of $f_U$ to each $V_j$ has $\mathcal P$.* Fix $j$ and write $i=i_j$. (a) The open immersion $e_j:V_j\hookrightarrow S_i$ is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism]: its local homomorphisms $\mathcal O_{S_i,e_j(v)}\to\mathcal O_{V_j,v}$ are isomorphisms, since an open subscheme has the local rings of the ambient scheme [def-pc-scheme], [def-weil-open-immersion]. (b) By condition (1) applied to $f_i$ (which has $\mathcal P$) and the flat $e_j$, the second projection of the fibre product $(X\times_SS_i)\times_{S_i}V_j\to V_j$ has $\mathcal P$. (c) By [lem-weil-pbc-open-preimage-fibre-product] applied to $f_i$ and the open $V_j\subseteq S_i$, the open subscheme $Y_j:=f_i^{-1}(V_j)\subseteq X\times_SS_i$ with the restriction $f_i|:Y_j\to V_j$ is also a fibre product of $f_i$ and $e_j$; by uniqueness of fibre products up to unique isomorphism compatible with the projections [def-pc-fibre-product] and condition (0) (with $b=\mathrm{id}_{V_j}$), $f_i|:Y_j\to V_j$ has $\mathcal P$. (d) The square of $f_i|$, $e_j$ sits on top of the cartesian square of $f$ and $g_i$ (projections $X\times_SS_i\to X$ and $f_i$); by [lem-weil-pbc-cartesian-square-pasting] the outer rectangle is cartesian: $Y_j$, with $Y_j\to X$ and $f_i|$, is a fibre product of $f$ and $g_ie_j:V_j\to S$.

proof.text: *The base change of $f_U$ along $h$ has $\mathcal P$.* Let $X'=X_U\times_UU'$ be the fibre product of $f_U$ and $h$ [def-pc-fibre-product], with second projection $p:X'\to U'$. Fix $j$ and let $W_j=\iota_j(V_j)\subseteq U'$, an open subset; by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-iso-onto-image] there is an isomorphism $\varphi_j:V_j\to W_j$ with $(W_j\hookrightarrow U')\circ\varphi_j=\iota_j$. (a) By [lem-weil-pbc-open-preimage-fibre-product] (for $p$ and $W_j$), $p^{-1}(W_j)$ with the restriction $p|:p^{-1}(W_j)\to W_j$ is a fibre product of $p$ and $W_j\hookrightarrow U'$; pasted on the cartesian square of $f_U$ and $h$ it gives, by [lem-weil-pbc-cartesian-square-pasting], that $p^{-1}(W_j)$ with $p^{-1}(W_j)\to X_U$ and $p|$ is a fibre product of $f_U$ and $h|_{W_j}:W_j\to U$. (b) By [lem-weil-pbc-open-preimage-fibre-product] (for $f$ and $U$), $X_U$ with $X_U\hookrightarrow X$ and $f_U$ is a fibre product of $f$ and $U\hookrightarrow S$; pasting the square of (a) on top of it [lem-weil-pbc-cartesian-square-pasting], $p^{-1}(W_j)$ with $p^{-1}(W_j)\to X$ and $p|$ is a fibre product of $f$ and $(U\hookrightarrow S)\circ h|_{W_j}:W_j\to S$. (c) Precomposing the second projection with $\varphi_j$ is an isomorphism of the data: $p^{-1}(W_j)$ with $p^{-1}(W_j)\to X$ and $\varphi_j^{-1}\circ p|$ is a fibre product of $f$ and $(U\hookrightarrow S)\circ h\circ\iota_j=(U\hookrightarrow S)\circ h_j=g_ie_j$ (immediate from the universal property [def-pc-fibre-product], since $\varphi_j$ is an isomorphism and $h|_{W_j}\varphi_j=h\iota_j=h_j$). (d) By step 4(d), $Y_j$ with $Y_j\to X$ and $f_i|$ is another fibre product of $f$ and $g_ie_j$; by uniqueness of fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product] there is an isomorphism $a:Y_j\to p^{-1}(W_j)$ with $\varphi_j^{-1}\circ p|\circ a=f_i|$, i.e. $p|\circ a=\varphi_j\circ f_i|$. By condition (0) (with $b=\varphi_j$) and step 4(c), $p|:p^{-1}(W_j)\to W_j$ has $\mathcal P$. (e) The $W_j$, $j=1,\dots,n$, cover $U'$ [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family], so by condition (2), $p:X'\to U'$ has $\mathcal P$.

proof.text: *Descent along $h$.* $U$ and $U'$ are affine, $h:U'\to U$ is flat and surjective (step 3), and the second projection $p:X_U\times_UU'\to U'$ of the fibre product of $f_U$ and $h$ has $\mathcal P$ (step 5). By condition (3) (with $S=U$, $S'=U'$, $g=h$ and the morphism $f_U:X_U\to U$), $f_U$ has $\mathcal P$. (If the fibre product used in condition (3) is the chosen one and $X'$ another, condition (0) transports $\mathcal P$ through the unique isomorphism over $U'$ [def-pc-fibre-product].)

proof.text: *Conclusion.* By steps 2-6, $f_U:f^{-1}(U)\to U$ has $\mathcal P$ for every affine open $U\subseteq S$; the affine opens cover $S$ [def-pc-scheme], so by condition (2), as reduced to in step 1, $f$ has $\mathcal P$.
